slides.title: Uni-VLaT: Whole-Body Tactile Adaptation of VLA Policies for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
slides.tldr: WHOLE-BODY TACTILE ADAPTATION FOR VLA POLICIES
slides.highlight: Uni-VLaT integrates distributed tactile sensing into vision-language-action policies to improve humanoid loco-manipulation and human-robot contact. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Uni-VLaT adapts pretrained VLA policies for humanoid loco-manipulation using whole-body tactile sensing and predictive supervision.
card.key_idea: Integrates distributed tactile tokens into a VLA policy, using a tactile-anchored multimodal context to predict future tactile, proprioceptive, and visual latent representations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on five real-robot tasks using Unitree G1; achieved 75% average success rate, outperforming non-tactile baselines by 43 points.
card.limitation: Sensors are sensitive to noise and mounting variations; limited whole-body tactile simulation restricts large-scale robustness studies.

slides.title: A robust single-sensing-element tactile sensor for concurrent pressure and tackiness detection with real-time signal decoupling capability
slides.tldr: BIMODAL TACTILE SENSING FOR PRESSURE AND TACKINESS
slides.highlight: This research introduces a tactile sensor capable of decoupling pressure and tackiness signals, supporting the multimodal social perception goals of HyECHO by enhancing robotic cognition of object surface characteristics.

card.one_liner: A single-element tactile sensor that decouples pressure and tackiness signals using a magneto-mechanical mechanism.
card.key_idea: A Hall effect sensor and soft magnetic composite in an elastic framework detect surface indentation (pressure) and bulging (pull-off force) to separate multimodal signals.

slides.title: HACo: Learning Haptic Active Compliance for Force-Aware Dexterous Manipulation
slides.tldr: HAPTIC ACTIVE COMPLIANCE FOR DEXTEROUS MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: HACo learns force-regulating actions by combining fingertip tactile and joint-torque feedback, achieving an 83% success rate across diverse force-sensitive tasks.

card.one_liner: HACo learns force-regulating dexterous manipulation by combining complementary tactile and joint-torque feedback with compliant actions.
card.key_idea: Uses compliance-regulated teleoperation for action targets, auxiliary compliant-intent supervision, and a Compliance Grounding Module with gated haptic cross-attention to integrate tactile and torque features.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on five real-world force-sensitive tasks (e.g., balloon drawing, cap unscrewing) over 20 trials; achieved 83% mean success rate versus 35% for T-Rex.
card.limitation: Relies on teleoperation for data, bounding policies to demonstrable motions and lacking intentional human force strategies.

slides.title: Kinematic Nonlinear Spatio-Temporal Trajectory Warping for Contact-Rich Dexterous Manipulation Demonstrations
slides.tldr: NONLINEAR TRAJECTORY WARPING FOR DEXTEROUS MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This method repurposes contact-rich dexterous manipulation demonstrations by using contact distributions to compute high-dimensional hand trajectories based on object-centric warp specifications.

card.one_liner: A method for repurposing contact-rich dexterous manipulation demonstrations via nonlinear spatio-temporal trajectory warping.
card.key_idea: A two-stage object-centric pipeline that first warps the object trajectory to fit constraints, then recovers hand poses using contact distributions via IK optimization.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 12 variations from 4 GRAB dataset demonstrations; results show hand-object spatial relationships preserved within 1mm on average using CPU-only processing.
card.limitation: Assumes rigid objects and convex barriers; fails to interpolate contact distributions for rapid finger movements or fine-grained contact changes.

slides.title: Rho: A Foundation for Efficiently Adaptable VLA Models
slides.tldr: ADAPTABLE VLA MODELS FOR BIMANUAL MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: Rho introduces a family of open-weights VLA models for bimanual manipulation that utilize embodiment midtraining and an internal latent policy for efficient online adaptation from corrective feedback.

card.one_liner: Rho is a 5B-parameter VLA family for bimanual manipulation designed for data-efficient task adaptation.
card.key_idea: A Phi-family VLM backbone coupled with a flow-matching action expert, using a multi-stage recipe: multi-embodiment pretraining, embodiment-specific midtraining, and task-specific finetuning.
card.evaluation: Evaluated in RoboTwin, LIBERO, and RoboEval simulations and on physical robots (YAM Box, UR AI Trainer, FR3 Duo) against open-weights VLAs.

slides.title: Urgent Actions Go First: Urgency-Aware Denoising for Real-Time VLA Control
slides.tldr: ACCELERATING VLA CONTROL VIA URGENCY-AWARE DENOISING
slides.highlight: Urgency-Aware Denoising (UAD) reduces inference latency in VLA policies by allocating computation based on action execution urgency, achieving up to a 1.89x speedup in action availability.

card.one_liner: UAD reduces VLA inference latency by releasing urgent actions early and overlapping tail denoising with execution.
card.key_idea: Allocates heterogeneous denoising budgets based on execution urgency, using Trajectory Reconciliation to maintain coherence and Ghost Action Correction to compensate for early-release errors.
card.evaluation: Tested on SmolVLA and π0.5 across LIBERO-Plus, Meta-World+, and real-world Dobot Nova2; achieved up to 1.89x speedup with comparable success rates.
card.limitation: Ghost Action Correction is only applicable when action dimensions admit compensation across consecutive control steps.

slides.title: EgoHumanoid-V2: Human-to-Humanoid Transfer of Coordinated Whole-Body Skills for Loco-Manipulation
slides.highlight: This framework enables the transfer of coordinated whole-body loco-manipulation skills from human demonstrations to humanoid robots. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied learning and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: EgoHumanoid-V2 enables zero-shot transfer of coordinated whole-body loco-manipulation skills from egocentric human demonstrations.
card.key_idea: A coarse-to-fine action alignment pipeline combining kinematic reference correction with dynamics-aware refinement, paired with robot-arm rendering and image augmentation to bridge the visual embodiment gap.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on four real-world tasks using a Unitree G1; achieved 51.67% mean score with 200 demonstrations, comparable to teleoperation data but with 76.36% less labor.
card.limitation: Alignment can still produce unstable motions, and the use of IK and repeated rollouts limits processing throughput.

slides.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Vision-Language-Action Models via Reinforced Fine Tuning
slides.tldr: REINFORCED FINE TUNING FOR COOPERATIVE MULTI-AGENT VLAs
slides.highlight: This research introduces a reinforced fine-tuning pipeline to improve coordination in multi-agent Vision-Language-Action models, supporting the MIMIC goal of simulating and analyzing hybrid human-AI societies through advanced agent models.

card.one_liner: A three-stage reinforced fine-tuning pipeline to improve coordination in multi-agent Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models.
card.key_idea: Combines initialization-aware data collection, offline credit-filtered tuning for per-agent advantage, and online RL in the VLA's latent noise space to stabilize training.
card.evaluation: Tested on 11 tasks (RoboTwin, RoboFactory, real-world Franka robots) using π0 and π0.5 backbones; success rates improved by 16.4% to 44%.
card.limitation: VLAs remain brittle to variations in initial conditions, requiring targeted human demonstrations to bootstrap learning in zero-success regions.
